groups.sentence: Instructors get prior approval before using AI or software to assist with grading, and use only approved or university-licensed tools.
Instructors let students opt out of AI-assisted grading and review their work instead, without penalty.
Instructors review and correct AI-generated feedback and findings themselves, keeping a human in the loop and remaining responsible for the result.
Instructors take extra review, consultation or caution before using AI to grade or assess student work.
Instructors may use AI to help draft formative feedback, flag patterns and generate ideas, provided they personalize the feedback.
Instructors do not rely on AI as the primary source of feedback, automate full feedback, or use it for grading written work.
Instructors do not use AI to grade or input student work without students' prior approval.
Instructors use AI feedback mainly for low-stakes or ungraded assignments.
Instructors create a quality assurance process so AI grading tools produce accurate, explainable and defendable grades, and avoid tools that cannot be validated.
AI grading has limits and ethical concerns, though some tools can ease grading, and student data privacy matters.
